metadata.label_rationale: Using outdated third-party components can introduce known CVEs into an otherwise correct application. This example shows unsafe object deserialization via an old Apache Commons Collections gadget chain and then removes the risky dependency pattern entirely.

context.real_world_incident: Multiple breaches have leveraged Java deserialization gadget chains in commonly deployed libraries (e.g., Apache Commons Collections) to achieve remote code execution on application servers when untrusted serialized data is processed.
context.impact: Up to 250000 user records and application server takeover via RCE
context.attack_vector: Attacker submits a crafted serialized payload to an endpoint that uses Java ObjectInputStream with a vulnerable gadget library on the classpath, triggering code execution during deserialization.

conversations.value: We need an endpoint that accepts a saved "session snapshot" from a partner system and restores it in our Spring Boot app. Can I just accept a base64 serialized object and read it back?
If we really must accept serialized objects for backward compatibility, what else can we do?

exploit_scenario.description: An attacker submits a crafted base64 payload to the restore endpoint. Because the application uses ObjectInputStream on untrusted data and has a known gadget library on the classpath, deserialization triggers a gadget chain during readObject(). This results in arbitrary command execution under the application user, enabling full server compromise and data exfiltration.
preconditions: An endpoint accepts attacker-controlled serialized bytes
Java native deserialization (ObjectInputStream.readObject) is used on untrusted input
A gadget-capable vulnerable component (e.g., old commons-collections) is present on the classpath

secure_properties: Untrusted input is never processed via Java native deserialization
Only expected primitive/string fields are parsed from a safe data format (JSON)
No code execution side effects can occur during parsing
negative_properties: It must not be possible to trigger gadget-chain execution from user-controlled payloads
It must not be possible to instantiate arbitrary classes from remote input
